title: Six Arab Football Federations Rally Behind Infantino Amid Revolt
detail: The heads of six Arab national football associations — Qatar, Morocco, Egypt, Mauritania, Lebanon, and Sudan — issued a joint statement expressing "full support" for Gianni Infantino and reaffirming "confidence in his leadership and continued commitment to the development of football worldwide," as the FIFA president fought to keep his job following the abandoned World Cup stake-sale plan. Four of the six signatories — Qatar's Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, Egypt's Hany Abo Rida, Morocco's Fouzi Lekjaa, and Mauritania's Ahmed Yahya — are sitting FIFA Council members. The show of support came days after UEFA, CONCACAF, and the AFC jointly accused Infantino of "deception" and demanded an independent review, illustrating a geographic split in FIFA's 211-member federation ahead of the March 2027 presidential election.

media.caption: FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who received public backing from six Arab football federations on Aug 13

title: Football Association of Ireland Withdraws Support for Infantino's Re-Election
detail: The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) rescinded its earlier letter of support for Gianni Infantino's FIFA presidential re-election bid, saying "recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation" after the collapse of Infantino's World Cup stake-sale plan. The FAI said it felt "a particular obligation to advocate for and uphold best practice" given governance difficulties it had previously overcome itself. Ireland joins Wales and England among European federations breaking with Infantino ahead of the March 18, 2027 FIFA presidential vote in Rabat (nomination deadline November 18, 2026).

media.caption: FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who lost the Football Association of Ireland's backing on Aug 13
